name: Learn basic woodworking joints
blurb: Four joints — butt, lap, dado and a simple mortise and tenon — cover most beginner projects and teach the accurate marking and sawing that everything else depends on.
gear: A handsaw and a chisel set
A marking gauge, square and pencil
steps: Learn to mark accurately: a sharp knife line beats a pencil line, and a square used consistently from one reference face avoids compounding error.
Learn to saw to a line, on the waste side, keeping the cut square in both planes.
Cut a butt joint reinforced with screws or dowels — simple, and it teaches squareness.
Cut a half-lap joint, which introduces removing material to a precise depth with a chisel.
Cut a dado or housing joint for shelving.
Cut a simple mortise and tenon, the joint that teaches real precision, and fit it so it needs a mallet tap but not force.
tips: Sharpen the chisels first. Blunt chisels crush rather than cut, and are far more dangerous.
Mark the waste side clearly. Sawing on the wrong side of the line is the classic beginner loss.
Test-fit dry before glue, every time.
proof: Four joints cut by hand, each square and tight enough to hold together before glue.
